text:
Voice and Tone

Macys speaks to the customer the way a trusted friend would. Warm, confident, occasionally playful. The voice should feel like someone who genuinely loves the product and wants the customer to feel good walking out of the store or closing their cart. Avoid corporate stiffness, avoid hard sell. The customer should never feel pressured.

Tone shifts by occasion. Holiday campaigns lean joyful and celebratory. Beauty leans intimate and discovery oriented. Home leans practical and aspirational. Workwear leans capable and modern.

Approved Taglines

The following taglines are pre approved for use in any campaign without further sign off:

* The Magic of Macys
* Find Your Magic
* Star Rewards, Every Day
* New In Store, New Online

Any tagline outside this list requires Brand Marketing Council review before it appears in production creative.

Banned Words and Phrases

The following terms are not permitted in any Macys campaign creative. They conflict with brand positioning or have been flagged by Legal in prior reviews.

* cheap
* basic
* last chance
* clearance blowout
* dirt cheap
* unbeatable
* lowest prices anywhere
* nobody beats Macys

If a campaign requires urgency language, use "ends Sunday", "limited time", or "while supplies last" instead.

Pricing Language

All pricing claims must follow the standard format below. This format was negotiated with Legal in 2024 and is required for compliance with state consumer protection laws.

* For range claims, write "Up to 40 percent off" never "40% off" alone.
* For tiered claims, always include the minimum: "Up to 40 percent off, starting at 10 percent off."
* Never use "free" without specifying conditions in the same line of copy.
* Never use "save big" or "huge savings" as the primary headline.

Visual Standards

The Macys star is the only protected logo mark. It must appear in either the official red (PMS 186, hex C8102E) or black, never recolored. Minimum clear space around the star is equal to one star height. The star may not be tilted, outlined, or filled with imagery.

Color Palette

* Primary red: hex C8102E
* Charcoal: hex 2E2E2E
* Soft cream: hex F5EFE6
* Accent gold for Holiday: hex C4A052

Seasonal palettes are released quarterly by the Creative Council. Anything outside the approved palette requires explicit approval.

Typography

* Headlines: Helvetica Neue Bold or the seasonal display font issued by Creative
* Body: Helvetica Neue Regular at 14 pt minimum on digital, 10 pt minimum on print
* Disclaimers: 8 pt minimum, never below the legal threshold for the channel

Updates

This document is reviewed twice a year by the Brand Marketing Council. To request a change (a new tagline, a banned word addition, a color palette update), file a request through the Brand portal with a specific example and rationale. The Council meets the second Tuesday of each month.

Purpose

This policy defines who must review and approve a campaign before it goes live. The intent is to keep approval predictable, reduce last minute escalations, and make sure the right experts see the right work at the right time.

Standard Approval Tiers

Every campaign moves through the following baseline reviewers in order:

1. Marketing Manager (the campaign owner submits)
2. Brand Review (voice, visual, tagline compliance)
3. Channel Lead (email, paid social, site, print as applicable)
4. Marketing Director sign off

A campaign cannot move to production until all four baseline tiers have signed off.

Special Case Reviewers

The following triggers add reviewers on top of the baseline tiers.

### Spend Threshold

Campaigns with total media spend over $500,000 require VP of Marketing plus Legal review. The VP review focuses on portfolio fit and budget allocation. Legal focuses on disclosure and pricing claims.

### New SKUs

Any campaign featuring a SKU that has not previously appeared in Macys marketing creative within the previous 24 months requires Merchandising sign off. Merchandising confirms inventory depth, pricing alignment, and vendor MAP compliance.

### Regulated Regions

Campaigns running in New York or California require Legal review regardless of spend. Both states have heightened consumer protection statutes (the New York Attorney General settlement on "compare at" pricing being the most cited reference) and Legal must clear all pricing language before launch.

### Sweepstakes or Contest

Any campaign that includes a prize, drawing, or contest mechanic requires Legal plus Compliance review. Bonded states (FL, NY, RI) require additional filings handled by Legal.

Service Level Agreements

* Standard approval: 3 business days from submission to final sign off
* High spend approval (over $500K): 5 business days
* Sweepstakes approval: 7 business days (allow time for bond filings)
* Regulated region approval: 5 business days

If a reviewer does not respond within the window, the campaign owner should escalate to the reviewer's manager, then to Marketing Operations.

Escalation Path

Stuck approvals escalate in this order:

1. Reviewer's direct manager
2. Marketing Operations approval queue lead
3. VP of Marketing
4. CMO (only for issues stalled more than 10 business days)

Out of Hours

Reviewers are not expected to approve campaigns outside business hours. Campaigns submitted Friday after 3 PM ET are considered received the following Monday.

Pre Clearance

The single biggest predictor of a clean approval cycle is pre clearing contentious items with Brand and Legal at campaign kickoff, before the first creative draft is built. Pre clearance is not a substitute for formal review, but it reduces rework dramatically and is strongly recommended for any campaign with a multiplier offer, comparative claim, financing offer, or new tagline.

Purpose

This document lists the legal disclaimers that must appear in Macys campaign creative. It is updated as regulations change. When in doubt, route the campaign to Legal review before publishing.

Star Rewards

Any creative that mentions Star Rewards points, tier benefits, or member exclusive offers must include the following at minimum:

"Star Rewards program subject to terms. See macys.com/starrewards for details."

If the campaign mentions a specific points multiplier (for example, "earn 5x points"), the qualifying categories and time window must appear in the same disclaimer block. Example:

"Earn 5x Star Rewards points on Beauty purchases. Valid March 1 through March 31, 2026. See terms at macys.com/starrewards."

Macys Credit Card and Financing

Any mention of the Macys Credit Card, deferred interest, or zero percent financing requires the following disclaimer in the same creative unit:

"Subject to credit approval. See application for important details on rates, fees, terms, and conditions. Credit issued by Citibank, N.A."

For deferred interest offers, the additional Truth in Lending Act language must appear: "Interest will be charged to your account from the purchase date if the promotional balance is not paid in full within the promotional period."

Pricing Claims

### Up To Claims

Any "up to X percent off" claim must include the minimum discount available in the offer. Example: "Up to 40 percent off, starting at 10 percent off."

This is required by Federal Trade Commission guidance on representative pricing claims.

### Compare At Pricing

Following the 2024 New York Attorney General settlement, any "compare at" or "original price" claim must reflect a price at which the item was offered for a meaningful period within the prior 90 days. If the comparison price was a manufacturer suggested retail price rather than a Macys offered price, the disclaimer must read:

"Compare at price reflects the manufacturer suggested retail price. Item may not have been sold at this price."

Comparative Claims

Claims that compare Macys pricing to competitors (for example, "save more than at competitor X") are not permitted without prior Legal review and documentation of the comparison methodology. Legal must approve the source data and the time window for the comparison.

Endorsement Disclosures

Any creative featuring a celebrity, influencer, or partner endorsement must include the connection disclosure:

"Paid partnership" or "Macys partner" tag on social posts and a visible disclosure on landing pages.

If the endorser received free product, the disclosure must read "Gifted by Macys" instead of "Paid partnership."

Sweepstakes

Sweepstakes creative must include the following:

* No purchase necessary
* Void where prohibited
* Odds depend on number of entries
* End date and time including time zone
* Full rules link

Sizing of Disclaimers

Disclaimers must be at least 8 point on print, 10 point on digital, and clearly legible against background. Disclaimers may not be hidden, faded, or placed off canvas. On video, disclaimers must remain on screen for at least 4 seconds and be paired with a stable background color where possible.

Escalation

When Legal cannot resolve a disclaimer question within the SLA, escalate to the Marketing Counsel lead. For matters touching active settlements (the New York compare at settlement, the California financing review), escalate to Marketing Counsel plus the Compliance Officer.

Purpose

This document defines how promotional discounts can be combined, what categories are excluded from promotions, and how vendor MAP rules apply.

Stackable Discounts

The default stacking order, where allowed, is:

1. Storewide promotion (for example, Friends and Family)
2. Category promotion (for example, 25 percent off Home)
3. Star Rewards member offer
4. Coupon code

When two storewide offers run simultaneously, only the higher discount applies. They do not stack.

Phrase Meaning

"Cannot be combined with other offers" means the offer in question may not stack with any other promotional discount or coupon. It does not block the customer from applying Star Rewards points redemption (which is treated as currency, not a discount).

"Excludes select brands" requires a linked list of excluded brands in the same creative or footer.

Exclusions

The following categories are typically excluded from storewide promotions. Confirm with Merchandising before each campaign, as exclusions can change by season.

* Fine Jewelry (above $1,000 ticket)
* Fragrance, with exceptions for promotional sets
* Beauty prestige (Lancome, Estee Lauder, Clinique, Dior Beauty, La Mer)
* Watches (Gucci, Tag Heuer)
* Designer Handbags (Coach, Kate Spade, Michael Kors above $500)
* Levi's
* Vendor restricted items flagged by Merchandising

Brands Under Strict MAP

The following brands enforce minimum advertised price under their vendor agreements. Discounts on these brands require written Merchandising approval and are typically only available during vendor sponsored events.

* Levi's
* Coach (above $500 ticket)
* Lancome
* Estee Lauder
* Clinique
* La Mer
* Dior Beauty
* Tag Heuer

A campaign that violates MAP can result in vendor charge backs and, in repeat cases, loss of the vendor account. This is the single most cited reason for emergency creative pulls.

Blackout Dates

Promotional creative may not run during the following windows without explicit Pricing Strategy approval:

* The week before and during a major brand event (for example, Lancome Friends and Family)
* Black Friday week, except for the approved Black Friday promotion plan
* Memorial Day week, except for the approved Memorial Day plan
* Vendor event windows published in the seasonal Merchandising calendar

Markdown Cadence

Once an item enters markdown, the cadence follows the standard merch playbook:

1. First markdown at 20 percent off, held for 14 days
2. Second markdown at 33 percent off, held for 14 days
3. Final markdown at 50 percent off until sell through
4. Clearance below 50 percent only with Pricing Strategy approval

Markdown items may not be promoted as "new" or "just arrived" in marketing creative. Markdown items also may not appear in primary hero positions on the site or email without Pricing Strategy notice.

Inventory Linked Promotions

If a promotion depends on inventory depth at a specific store or distribution center, the campaign owner must confirm inventory with Merchandising no earlier than 5 business days before launch. Inventory snapshots older than 5 days are considered stale.

Purpose

Every asset uploaded to the Macys Digital Asset Management system (DAM) must be tagged according to this policy. Proper tagging is what allows the Marketing, Merchandising, and Creative teams to find and reuse assets without recreating work. It also protects Macys from rights violations when models, photographers, or licensed properties are involved.

Required Metadata Fields

Every asset must have the following fields populated at upload time. Assets missing any required field will be quarantined and will not surface in search.

* **Category**: top level (Apparel, Beauty, Home, Jewelry, Kids)
* **Subcategory**: more specific (Womens Apparel, Mens Apparel, Skincare, Fragrance, Bedding, etc)
* **Season**: SP25, SU25, FA25, HO25, etc
* **Model Rights Expiration**: the date the model release expires
* **Region Usage Rights**: which regions the asset may be used in (US, Canada, Puerto Rico, Restricted)
* **Photographer Credit**: full name and agency
* **Retouch Level**: minimal, standard, heavy (used by Brand to determine where the asset can appear)
* **Brand or Vendor**: if the asset features a specific brand SKU
* **Shoot Date**: original capture date

Model Release Rule (90 Day Buffer)

Any asset featuring an identifiable model expires from active use 90 days before the model release expiration date, not on the expiration date itself. This 90 day buffer was added in 2024 after the Q3 incident where a model release lapsed mid campaign and creative had to be replaced inside 48 hours.

When an asset enters the 90 day window, the DAM flags it amber. When it enters the 30 day window, it flags red and is removed from active search results. Renewing a model release requires Creative Operations to initiate the renewal at least 60 days before the amber flag.

Asset Flagging Process

If a user finds a degraded, low resolution, or unusable asset in the DAM, the user files a flag through the DAM portal. The flag captures:

* Asset ID
* Issue type (resolution, color, retouch, rights, other)
* Free text description
* Urgency (standard, high)

Creative Operations triages flags daily. Standard flags resolve within 5 business days. High urgency flags resolve within 1 business day.

Restricted Use Cases

Assets tagged "Restricted" may not be used outside the explicit purpose listed in the asset notes. Common restricted cases include:

* Vendor sponsored shoots where the vendor retains shared rights
* Influencer collaborations with specific channel limits (Instagram only, no paid media, etc)
* Editorial features with one time use agreements

Using a restricted asset outside its agreement triggers a rights violation review by Legal.

Resolution Threshold

After the Q4 2025 holiday incident where four key Beauty assets were ingested at degraded resolution and had to be rebuilt, the DAM enforces a minimum resolution check at upload. Assets below 300 DPI for print intent or below 2400 pixels on the long edge for digital intent are rejected at upload with a clear error message and a link to the reshoot request form.

Tag Hygiene

Tag quality drifts over time. Creative Operations runs a quarterly tag audit and reaches out to original uploaders for clarification. Assets that remain mis tagged after the audit are quarantined until corrected.

Purpose

Macys serves customers across the continental US, Puerto Rico, and a small but growing Canadian footprint. Campaign copy must adapt to regional language, holidays, and pricing without losing brand voice. This guide defines the expectations.

Spanish Localization (Texas, Florida, Puerto Rico)

All Texas, Florida, and Puerto Rico campaigns must ship a Spanish version alongside English. The Spanish version is not a literal translation. It is a transcreation that preserves brand voice, warmth, and intent.

Key conventions:

* Use neutral Latin American Spanish, not Castilian
* Star Rewards is translated as "Premios Star" (a fixed translation, do not vary)
* "Up to 40 percent off" translates to "Hasta 40 por ciento de descuento"
* "Starting at 10 percent off" translates to "Desde 10 por ciento de descuento"
* Avoid English borrowings where a clean Spanish equivalent exists (use "oferta" rather than "deal")
* Puerto Rico copy should reference local holidays where the calendar overlaps (see Regional Holidays below)

Translations are reviewed by the in market Macys Spanish editor, not by an outside vendor alone, before campaign launch. Following the Q4 2025 Holiday typo incident in Puerto Rico signage, Spanish creative is now reviewed twice, once at copy lock and once at final asset before any print or production run.

French Canadian

Any creative running in Quebec or in cross border campaigns reaching Canadian customers requires a French Canadian version. Use Quebec French, not France French. Key conventions:

* Star Rewards translates as "Recompenses Star"
* Pricing follows Canadian dollar with currency code (CAD)
* Quebec consumer protection rules require both languages on any paid out of home placement

Regional Pricing

Pricing in Puerto Rico is set in US dollars but may differ from continental US pricing on certain categories (notably Beauty and Fragrance) due to shipping and tariff costs. Always pull the regional price from the Pricing Strategy regional table, never assume the continental price applies.

Canadian pricing is in CAD and follows the Canada Pricing table maintained by Pricing Strategy.

section: Star Rewards Tier Names by Region
text:
Star Rewards Tier Names by Region

* Continental US: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum
* Puerto Rico: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platino
* Canada (English): Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum
* Canada (French): Bronze, Argent, Or, Platine

The Platino spelling for Puerto Rico is intentional and customer tested. Do not "correct" it back to Platinum.

Regional Holidays

The following holidays shift creative calendar planning by region. Confirm with Regional Marketing before scheduling campaigns near these dates.

* Three Kings Day (January 6) in Puerto Rico, treated as a primary gifting holiday equal to or larger than Christmas Eve. Creative should include Three Kings imagery and a gifting angle.
* Lunar New Year (date varies, late January or February) on the West Coast, particularly the San Francisco Bay Area and Greater Los Angeles. Beauty and Home see the largest lift.
* Dia de los Muertos (November 1 and 2) in Texas, Arizona, New Mexico, and Southern California, primarily a Home and Beauty moment.
* Quebec National Holiday (June 24) for any Canadian creative running through late June.

Summary

The Q4 2025 Holiday campaign closed with mixed results. Revenue against plan came in at 98 percent, a small miss driven by softer than expected Home performance in the final two weeks. The wins, misses, and action items below come from the retro session held January 12, 2026, with representatives from Marketing, Brand, Creative, Legal, and Merchandising.

Wins

### Beauty Loyalists Segment Outperformed

The Beauty Loyalists segment (customers who purchased prestige Beauty in the prior 12 months and held an active Star Rewards account) outperformed plan by 23 percent. Email open rate hit 41 percent (versus a 28 percent target) and conversion ran 1.6x the segment average. The team attributes this to the early November teaser series, which front loaded gift sets before the broader Holiday push and avoided the late November inbox crush.

### Cross Channel Consistency

Holiday creative held a consistent look across email, paid social, site, and out of home. The Brand audit scored the campaign at 4.6 out of 5, the highest score for any Holiday in three years.

### Star Rewards Multiplier Drove Repeat

The 5x Star Rewards weekend (December 6 through 8) drove a 34 percent lift in repeat purchase rate among existing members. Legal pre cleared the disclaimer two weeks ahead, which avoided the late approval risk seen in prior years.

Misses

### DAM Degradation Delayed Production

Four key Beauty assets uploaded in late October were flagged as low resolution mid November. Creative had to rebuild them, which pushed the second wave of email creative four days late and forced a rush approval cycle. Root cause was a DAM ingest issue where source files were down sampled on upload. Creative Operations confirmed the underlying ingest bug is patched but the team lost four production days.

### Two Disclaimers Flagged Late

Legal flagged two late stage disclaimers in the gift card creative (insufficient Truth in Lending disclosure on the deferred financing offer) on December 1. The fix required pulling the creative for 18 hours and reissuing. Postmortem traced this to a copy review that bypassed Legal during a holiday week stand in.

### Spanish Localization Typos

The Puerto Rico Spanish creative shipped with two typos in the headline (a missing accent on "ofertas" and an incorrect verb conjugation in the call to action). The market editor caught both, but the assets had already gone to print on a small run of in store signage, which had to be reprinted at a cost of approximately $12,000.

Action Items

1. DAM ingest validation. Creative Operations will require a resolution check at upload and reject assets below the production threshold. Owner: Creative Operations. Due: March 31, 2026.

2. Standing Legal review during holiday windows. Legal commits to a named primary reviewer plus a named backup for every holiday week, with handoff documented in writing. Owner: Marketing Counsel. Due: October 1, 2026 (ahead of Q4 2026).

3. Two stage Spanish review. All Spanish creative must be reviewed by the in market Macys Spanish editor twice, once at copy lock and once at final asset before any print or production run. Owner: Localization Council. Due: immediate, starting February 2026 campaigns.

4. Comparative claim methodology library. Build a reusable methodology library for year over year claims so future campaigns are not blocked by Legal on the basis of missing comparison data. Owner: Marketing Counsel plus Marketing Operations. Due: May 1, 2026.

Summary

The Spring 2025 Beauty launch ran March 3 through April 15, anchored by the "Find Your Glow" creative platform. Sarah Chen led the campaign with support from the Beauty Merchandising team. Revenue came in 7 percent ahead of plan, driven primarily by skincare and fragrance gift sets. Below are the key learnings.

Performance

* Total campaign revenue: $42.1M (plan was $39.3M)
* Email open rate: 32 percent (segment average 26 percent)
* Paid social ROAS: 4.2 (target was 3.5)
* In store conversion: 18 percent uplift in Beauty department over comparable weeks in 2024

The Beauty Discovery segment (customers who had browsed but not purchased Beauty in the prior 90 days) was the standout. Conversion ran 2.1x the segment baseline. The team credits the sampling offer (free 3 product sample box with $50 purchase) as the primary driver.

Segment Learnings

### Beauty Loyalists

Already engaged. The Spring campaign confirmed that Beauty Loyalists respond best to product depth (full ingredient stories, founder content, ritual videos) rather than discount messaging. The 5 minute founder video for the new La Mer launch drove the highest watch through rate of any video in the campaign at 58 percent.

### Beauty Discovery

Responsive to sampling and education. Free samples plus a "how to start" guide outperformed pure discount creative by a wide margin. Sarah noted that the educational module on the landing page (which explained how to layer products) drove a 12 percent lift in average order value among Discovery segment buyers.

### Beauty Lapsed

Did not move. Lapsed Beauty customers (no purchase in 12 months) returned at roughly the baseline rate despite a dedicated reactivation email series. The team flagged that the offer (10 percent off) may not be enough to reactivate in a category where competitors are aggressive on discount.

Cross Channel Performance

* Email contributed 38 percent of attributed revenue
* Paid social contributed 22 percent
* Site (organic, search, push) contributed 31 percent
* Affiliate and partnerships contributed 9 percent

Email continued to over index, consistent with past Beauty campaigns. Paid social showed the largest year over year improvement, up from 17 percent contribution in Spring 2024.

section: What Sarah and the Team Would Do Differently
text:
What Sarah and the Team Would Do Differently

1. Move the sampling offer earlier in the campaign. The sampling offer launched in week three. By the time it landed, the cleanest segment overlap windows had passed. Next launch, lead with the sample, follow with the full collection story.

2. Pair the founder video with retargeting. The La Mer founder video had outstanding watch through but the team did not have a structured retarget for the watchers. Build the retarget plan into the creative kickoff for next launch.

3. Rethink the lapsed Beauty offer. Either deepen the discount, change the message away from price, or accept that this segment is not movable in the Spring window. Recommend testing a curated edit ("Sarah's Picks for the Customer Who Stepped Away") in Fall 2025.

4. Better localized creative. Texas and Florida Spanish creative was rushed in the final week. Localization should be on the master timeline from the kickoff meeting, not added at copy lock.

Ticket Summary

* **Campaign**: Memorial Day Home Category Push
* **Submitted by**: Sarah Chen
* **Submission date**: May 19, 2025 at 09:14 ET
* **Final approval**: May 23, 2025 at 17:42 ET (day 5)
* **Spend tier**: High ($612,000)
* **Special triggers**: VP plus Legal (over $500K threshold)

Activity Log

#### May 19, 2025 at 09:14 ET, Sarah Chen (Marketing Manager)

Submitted. Three email assets, two paid social variants, one site banner. Headline reads "Big savings on the home you love, this Memorial Day only." Comparative claim ("more savings than last year") flagged for Legal in the routing notes.

#### May 19, 2025 at 14:02 ET, Brand Review (Marcus Lee)

Approved with one comment. "Tagline is acceptable but borderline on 'big savings' language, see Brand Guidelines section on pricing language. Consider 'Save on the home you love' as a tighter alternative for the headline. Approving as is, flagging for future."

#### May 20, 2025 at 10:30 ET, VP Marketing (D. Patel), revision request 1

"Headline conflict with brand guidelines. 'Big savings' is not on the approved list and reads close to a banned phrase. Please revise to 'Save on the home you love' or similar before resubmitting. Also: confirm the comparative claim has Legal sign off on methodology."

#### May 20, 2025 at 15:48 ET, Sarah Chen, revision 1 submitted

Headline updated to "Save on the home you love, Memorial Day only." Comparative claim removed from the email creative, retained in one paid social variant pending Legal review.

#### May 21, 2025 at 11:20 ET, Legal (R. Owusu)

"Comparative claim in paid social variant 2 cannot run without a documented comparison methodology. We do not have a methodology on file for Home category year over year. Recommend removing the claim. Pricing disclaimer on email 2 is missing the minimum discount ('starting at X percent off') and must be added per Pricing Language standard."

#### May 21, 2025 at 16:55 ET, VP Marketing (D. Patel), revision request 2

"Agree with Legal. Remove the comparative claim from all variants. Add the starting at minimum to email 2. Resubmit once cleaned up."

#### May 22, 2025 at 09:33 ET, Sarah Chen, revision 2 submitted

Comparative claim removed from all paid social variants. Email 2 disclaimer updated to "Up to 40 percent off Home, starting at 15 percent off."

#### May 22, 2025 at 14:18 ET, Legal (R. Owusu)

Approved. Disclaimer reads cleanly.

#### May 22, 2025 at 16:40 ET, Channel Lead (J. Park)

Approved. Production timeline still on track for Memorial Day eve send.

#### May 23, 2025 at 17:42 ET, VP Marketing (D. Patel)

Final approved. Cleared for production. Note for retro: build the comparative claim methodology library before next Memorial Day so this does not block again.

Outcome

Approved on day 5 (within the high spend SLA for this tier). Campaign launched on schedule.

Lessons

The two revision cycles cost roughly three production days. Both were preventable. The "big savings" headline could have been caught at Brand review with a stronger initial revision rather than a comment plus approval. The comparative claim could have been caught at kickoff if Legal had been pre cleared on methodology. Both feed the retro action items.

Ticket Summary

* **Campaign**: February Beauty Refresh
* **Submitted by**: Priya Ramesh
* **Submission date**: February 9, 2026 at 10:02 ET
* **Final approval**: February 11, 2026 at 13:08 ET (day 2)
* **Spend tier**: Mid ($245,000)
* **Special triggers**: None

Activity Log

#### February 9, 2026 at 10:02 ET, Priya Ramesh (Marketing Manager)

Submitted. Two email assets, three paid social variants, one site refresh module. Headline "Your spring skin starts here." Star Rewards 3x multiplier featured. Disclaimers pre cleared with Legal in the kickoff meeting on January 27.

#### February 9, 2026 at 13:45 ET, Brand Review (Marcus Lee)

Approved. "Voice is on. Visual direction matches the Spring Beauty palette. No notes."

#### February 10, 2026 at 09:18 ET, Legal (R. Owusu)

Approved. "Star Rewards disclaimer reads cleanly. Multiplier window and qualifying category present. Pricing language is compliant."

#### February 10, 2026 at 11:30 ET, Channel Lead (J. Park)

Approved. "Production timeline confirmed with the Beauty channel calendar. No conflict."

#### February 11, 2026 at 13:08 ET, Marketing Director (T. Alvarez)

Final approved. "Clean submission, clean review cycle. Nice work to the team for pre clearing Legal at kickoff."

Outcome

Approved on day 2, well inside the standard 3 business day SLA. Campaign launched February 13, 2026.

Note for the team

This ticket is the model for how approval should run when Legal is pre cleared at kickoff. Priya brought the proposed Star Rewards disclaimer to the kickoff meeting, Legal signed off in principle on January 27, and the submission included the exact pre approved language. Total reviewer effort was minutes per reviewer rather than hours of back and forth. Worth replicating.

Submission Quality Checklist (used by Priya)

For reference, here is the pre submission checklist Priya used. It is not required, but it correlates strongly with two day approvals.

* All disclaimers pre cleared with Legal at kickoff
* Headline mapped to an approved tagline pattern or pre reviewed alternative
* Pricing language follows the standard format ("Up to X percent off, starting at Y percent off")
* Visual assets pulled from DAM with current model release and resolution checks passed
* Channel calendar confirmed with the Channel Lead before submission
* No banned words present (run a grep against the latest brand guidelines banned list)

Purpose

This document is a reference of real compliance flags raised on past Macys campaigns. Each example shows the flagged copy, the rule that was tripped, and the fix that landed in production. Use this when drafting new creative to anticipate where reviews tend to push back.

Examples

### Example 1, banned word "last chance"

* **Flagged copy**: "Last chance on Spring Beauty, ends Sunday."
* **Rule tripped**: BRAND-GL-2026-001, banned word list.
* **Fix**: "Spring Beauty, ends Sunday." (urgency carried by the date, not the phrase.)

### Example 2, "up to" missing minimum

* **Flagged copy**: "Up to 50 percent off Home Refresh."
* **Rule tripped**: BRAND-GL-2026-001 pricing language plus LEGAL-DIS-2026-002 FTC representative pricing.
* **Fix**: "Up to 50 percent off Home Refresh, starting at 20 percent off."

### Example 3, compare at price without 90 day basis

* **Flagged copy**: "Compare at $129, now $59."
* **Rule tripped**: LEGAL-DIS-2026-002, post 2024 NY AG settlement on compare at pricing.
* **Fix**: Either confirm and document the prior 90 day offer at $129, or change to "Manufacturer suggested retail price $129, our price $59" with the corresponding disclaimer.

### Example 4, "save big" headline

* **Flagged copy**: "Save big on Bedding this weekend."
* **Rule tripped**: BRAND-GL-2026-001, pricing language ("save big" not allowed as a primary headline).
* **Fix**: "Bedding refresh, 30 percent off this weekend."

### Example 5, financing offer without TILA language

* **Flagged copy**: "Zero percent financing for 12 months on purchases over $499."
* **Rule tripped**: LEGAL-DIS-2026-002, Macys Credit Card Truth in Lending disclosure.
* **Fix**: Same headline with the required disclaimer added in the same creative unit, including "Subject to credit approval" and the deferred interest language.

### Example 6, influencer post missing disclosure

* **Flagged copy**: Instagram post from partner influencer, "Loving my new Macys finds for fall."
* **Rule tripped**: LEGAL-DIS-2026-002, endorsement disclosure (FTC).
* **Fix**: Same post with "#MacysPartner" and "Paid partnership" tag visible in the post itself, not buried in the caption.

### Example 7, restricted asset reused

* **Flagged copy**: A Holiday gift guide reused a Lancome influencer collaboration asset for a non Beauty placement.
* **Rule tripped**: DAM-TAG-2025-005, restricted asset usage outside agreement.
* **Fix**: Asset pulled, replaced with a Macys owned alternative. Asset reuse request routed through Creative Operations for future shoots.

### Example 8, Spanish call to action missing accent

* **Flagged copy**: "Compra ya y ahorra mas."
* **Rule tripped**: LOC-STYLE-2025-002, neutral Latin American Spanish, missing accent.
* **Fix**: Same line corrected with the accented form of mas (the comparative adverb, accented). Two stage Spanish review now required per the Q4 2025 retro action item.

### Example 9, MAP brand discounted

* **Flagged copy**: "Levi's, 25 percent off this weekend."
* **Rule tripped**: PRICE-RULES-2026-001, Levi's is a MAP enforced brand.
* **Fix**: Creative pulled before launch. Promotional language replaced with "Shop Levi's, new arrivals." Pricing Strategy notified Merchandising.

### Example 10, sweepstakes missing rules

* **Flagged copy**: "Enter to win a $500 Macys gift card, sign up for emails today."
* **Rule tripped**: LEGAL-DIS-2026-002, sweepstakes required language (no purchase necessary, void where prohibited, odds, end date and time zone, full rules link).
* **Fix**: Sweepstakes mechanic relaunched with full rules linked, all required language present, plus the bonded state filings handled by Legal.

How to Use This Document

Run a quick scan of any draft headline and disclaimer block against this list before submitting for Brand or Legal review. Catching these issues at the draft stage saves an average of 1.5 review days per campaign based on the Q4 2025 to Q1 2026 data set.

Purpose

Common questions the Marketing Operations team gets every week. Answers reflect current practice, not aspirational policy. If something here conflicts with a posted policy document, the policy document wins, and please tell us so we can fix this FAQ.

section: How long does VP approval usually take?
text:
How long does VP approval usually take?

The SLA is 3 business days for standard tier and 5 business days for high spend (over $500K). In practice, the median is 2 days for standard and 4 days for high spend. The variability is mostly driven by whether you pre cleared the contentious items with Brand and Legal before submission. Campaigns that surface new questions at the VP stage routinely add 2 to 3 days. See TICKET-INC-2025-4471 for an example of a high spend ticket that took the full 5 days, and TICKET-INC-2026-0212 for a clean 2 day approval.

section: Can I run a campaign without Legal review?
text:
Can I run a campaign without Legal review?

Yes for the baseline path (no spend over $500K, no regulated region, no new SKU, no sweepstakes, no comparative claim, no Star Rewards multiplier, no financing offer). In practice this is most short notice site refresh creative and routine seasonal placements. If any of those triggers apply, Legal is required.

section: What if the DAM does not have the asset I need?
text:
What if the DAM does not have the asset I need?

First, search by category and season tags rather than free text. Many assets are mis tagged and a tag based search finds things free text misses. If you still cannot find what you need, file a creative request through Creative Operations and flag the campaign date. Creative Ops will either pull from an upcoming shoot, request a small reshoot, or recommend an alternative direction. Lead time is typically 10 business days for new creative, 3 business days for a pull from an upcoming shoot.

section: How do I escalate a stuck approval?
text:
How do I escalate a stuck approval?

The escalation path is: reviewer's manager first, Marketing Operations approval queue lead second, VP of Marketing third, CMO only for issues stalled more than 10 business days. Before escalating, please confirm the reviewer is not out of office (the approval tool sometimes does not surface this). Most "stuck" approvals are reviewers on PTO whose backup was never set.

section: Can I add Legal as a reviewer after submission?
text:
Can I add Legal as a reviewer after submission?

Yes, edit the routing on the existing ticket. You do not need to resubmit. The clock resets only if a new revision is uploaded after Legal is added.

section: What counts as a "new SKU" for Merchandising sign off?
text:
What counts as a "new SKU" for Merchandising sign off?

A SKU that has not appeared in any prior Macys marketing creative within the previous 24 months. Re launches, new colorways of an existing item, and new sizes of an existing item do not require Merchandising sign off unless flagged in the seasonal Merchandising calendar.

section: How do I find out if my brand is under MAP?
text:
How do I find out if my brand is under MAP?

Check PRICE-RULES-2026-001 for the standing MAP list. Brands are added throughout the year so the standing list may be out of date. When in doubt, ask Merchandising before you write the promo headline.

section: Who owns the post launch retro?
text:
Who owns the post launch retro?

The campaign manager owns scheduling and notes. Marketing Operations owns the retro template, action item tracking, and the closeout. Retros are due within 4 weeks of campaign close.

section: What if Legal pre cleared my copy but Brand later flagged it?
text:
What if Legal pre cleared my copy but Brand later flagged it?

Legal sign off does not satisfy Brand sign off. Brand can flag a Legal cleared piece for voice, visual, or tagline issues. Both must approve. If you hit a conflict between Legal and Brand recommendations, escalate to the VP of Marketing for the call.

section: Can I run a campaign in Puerto Rico without a Spanish version?
text:
Can I run a campaign in Puerto Rico without a Spanish version?

No. Spanish creative is required for any campaign running in Puerto Rico, Texas, or Florida. See LOC-STYLE-2025-002.

section: How do I add a new banned word to the brand guidelines?
text:
How do I add a new banned word to the brand guidelines?

Submit a request to the Brand Marketing Council. Bring a specific example of the word in use, the rationale (legal risk, brand fit, customer feedback), and a proposed replacement. The Council reviews monthly.
